new_entities.name: Post-workout whey protein intake
new_entities.description: Whey protein consumed after resistance exercise.

new_entities.name: Muscle protein synthesis
new_entities.description: The rate at which skeletal muscle builds new protein.

edges.effect_quant: Direct post-exercise studies show that even 10 g of whey plus carbohydrate increases muscle protein synthesis relative to carbohydrate alone, while 20 g activates mTOR signaling more strongly than 10 g, indicating a clear dose response within practical post-workout ranges.
edges.population: healthy young men, especially after resistance exercise
edges.mechanism: Whey is rapidly digested and delivers a leucine-rich amino acid pulse that activates anabolic signaling and provides substrate for muscle repair. That makes it particularly effective immediately after exercise, when muscle is sensitized to amino acid availability.
edges.summary: This is one of the stronger practical sports-nutrition edges. Post-workout whey reliably stimulates muscle protein synthesis, and the trial literature supports both the basic effect and a plausible dose response, even if the exact optimal dose varies by body size and training context.
edges.caveats: Most direct mechanistic studies are small and conducted in young men. The immediate muscle protein synthesis response is not the same as long-term hypertrophy, but it is one of the more robust short-term signals available for a protein supplement.

evidence.citation: TangJE et al 2007 Br J Nutr
evidence.notes: Minimal whey protein with carbohydrate stimulates muscle protein synthesis following resistance exercise in trained young men.

evidence.citation: KandaA et al 2014 Eur J Appl Physiol
evidence.notes: Whey protein intake after resistance exercise activates mTOR signaling in a dose-dependent manner in human skeletal muscle.
Whey Protein Supplementation Enhances Whole Body Protein Metabolism and Performance Recovery after Resistance Exercise: A Double-Blind Crossover Study.
